about: What each UI test does on a device, listed by scripts/test_ios_ui.sh --dry-run for approval (artifact/topics/ios-c-abi-2, UI automation design v4, 4.6). systemui: presses system alerts or the springboard. sharesheet: opens the share sheet of the harness and closes it with Close without choosing a target; nothing in the sheet is read on a device (Share UI test plan v3; Copy, the sheet's contents, backgrounding and Control Center are simulator only). clipboard: on a device, writes and observes a named pasteboard of the harness only and never reads or writes the general pasteboard (CB-5); the general-pasteboard tests CB-1 to CB-4 are simulator only (Clipboard test plan v4). reinstall: the harness is removed and installed again before the test. playertests: runs the iOS player tests of scripts/verify_unity_ios.sh with the UI driver next to them (the player's own alerts, the share sheet closed with Close, a test value typed into a text-input alert without a password field; Clipboard on named pasteboards only; a second run on a fresh install asks for the notification permission once, answers Allow, and opens the player's page in Settings and comes back; the full list is in scripts/ios_ui_runner.py). The entry PlayerTests/IosPlayer is that run; scripts/test_ios_ui.sh never selects it. simulatorOnly: tests never run on a device (the runner leaves them out of device runs and refuses to approve them): backgrounding, Control Center by coordinates, and login dialogs (password saving and AutoFill can take over the screen) - Dialog UI test plan v3. appdialog: presses the harness's own alerts and action sheets (not the springboard); ID-9 types a test value into a text field with the device keyboard. After the switch to the C ABI 2.0.0, the player tests and the UI tests run on a device only after they all pass on the simulator (a wrong migration could otherwise reach the user's device, for example a remove request to the general pasteboard; stage 3-R implementation review v1, R-11). Notification: keepInstalled lists, in order, the tests that run on a device only in the keep-installed run (scripts/test_ios_ui.sh --device --keep-installed; keep-installed design v4): the harness is installed once, NU-1 allows the permission, the run waits until the user lets only the harness through a Focus mode, and the rest run without reinstalling. focus and longpress describe that run. The other Notification tests are simulator only. timeLimits: a test's time limit in seconds when 600 is not enough (NU-11 took over 600 s on the iPhone XS). notMovedYet: the test classes of features not moved to the C ABI 2.0.0 yet (3-S design v3, 1.7). Their UI tests expect 1.x, which the package no longer has, so they are left out of every run (scripts/test_ios_ui.sh refuses them by name), and a class leaves the list when its feature moves (stage 3).
